why_this_exists: Owner, 2026-08-10: 提供するものは測定分析改善ループまわさないと需要のあるものになっていかない. Every loop in this repository measures the ROUTE — ETA, venues, findable surface, reach, usage, heartbeats. None took the offer itself as its subject, and state/portfolio.json has carried a field named not_examined since it was written. This file is the register the product loop runs on. scripts/product-loop.mjs derives loopability from it and pulse.yml runs the check hourly.
the_ladder_is_in_the_script: scripts/product-loop.mjs LADDER. Cheapest and fastest signal first: promise_conformance, stranger_reaction, sells_against, behaviour. The order is the design content — measuring conversion on an artifact that does not deliver what its page promises tells you about the promise, not the product.

offers.what: The priced product. USD 25, sold on Gumroad and listed on itch.io.
offers.source_finding: NO SOURCE TREE EXISTS IN ANY REPOSITORY THIS ACCOUNT OWNS. The four artifacts the live listing promises — brand.config.json, generator.html, validate_config.py, test_engine.py — return zero hits across four GitHub code searches, against a positive control (filename:KIT_VERSION) that returns hits inside a PRIVATE repository and therefore proves the index reaches them. A built ZIP plausibly exists as a Gumroad attachment; no source does. Full record: state/constraints.json the_product_itself_has_never_been_opened.the_attempt_to_open_it.

measurement.why_null: Every rung above `behaviour` needs the artifact. There is no artifact to open. This is not 'the round has not been run yet' — the round cannot be run, and that is the finding.

offers.what_this_costs_right_now: It cannot be inspected, tested, corrected, rebuilt or re-delivered. If a buyer reports it broken there is nothing to fix it in. Every surface change already made to it — copy, addressee, tags, cover, category, announcement — is unjudgeable, because the thing under the surface was never read. And the 2026-08-23 judgement was going to attribute a zero result to the venue.

the_two_ways_out_and_neither_is_free.rebuild_the_source: Write the four promised artifacts, in a repository we own, matching the live listing. Then the offer becomes loopable and every rung opens. Cost: real build work, on the binding resource.
the_two_ways_out_and_neither_is_free.retire_the_offer: Stop routing effort to it and put the loop behind something that already has a source. Cost: the listing work already done stops compounding — but it is not lost, because it was never judged in the first place.
the_two_ways_out_and_neither_is_free.do_not_choose_by_sunk_cost: The listing, cover, tags and announcement are already paid for and they are not evidence for either option. A14: 'it was already built' is not a reason.

offers.explicitly_not_claimed: That the product is bad. The owner's 中身見てないんだけどこれ絶対売れないと思うよ and any defence of it are equally unbacked. Nobody has opened it. That symmetry is the point — this is a statement about what can be measured, not a verdict on quality.

offers.what: The free, sign-up-free, single-file browser idle game. The entrance the route depends on.
offers.source_note: In this repository, checked by scripts/check-free-artifact.mjs on every pulse, and state/public-host.json verifies the published copy matches it. It is an ORIGINAL artifact the Codex lane wrote, not a cut-down of the kit — the two are routinely named in one breath and the relationship does not exist.

measurement.why_this_rung: promise_conformance is nearly vacuous here — a free demo promises almost nothing, so conformance would pass without telling us anything. The unanswered question is whether anyone who did not write it would play it twice, and that is answerable this week on the Codex pool for the cost of one INBOX task.
measurement.how: Hand the file to a reviewer who did not write it, blind to authorship, default verdict negative. Ask for a decision (would you keep playing / would you pay for more) plus the single strongest reason against. Not a rewrite, not a feature list — a verdict and a reason.
measurement.not_this_rung_yet: behaviour. state/findable-surface.json establishes the page is served noindex,nofollow and nothing links it, so a view count today measures our distribution, not the artifact. Reading a zero as 'nobody wants it' would be the same mistake as reading it as 'wrong venue'.

no_longer_queued.what_changed: Both .a and .b carry their done markers, so the lane was free for the first time since this offer was registered. The round is filed. The field it replaces said the round was task .b — it was not; .b went to the reach-scale question that decided the route, and this is .c.
no_longer_queued.how_the_blind_is_kept: The task carries the public URL and nothing else — no repository name, no authorship, no statement of why it is being asked. The lane WROTE assets/free-demo/index.html, so recognition is the live risk, and the task ends by asking outright whether the reviewer has seen it before, with 'yes' explicitly stated as not a penalty. A round that comes back recognised is VOID and must be discarded rather than kept.
no_longer_queued.why_the_public_URL_and_not_the_file: state/public-host.json verifies the published copy is byte-identical to the repo copy (sha256 646acbae1c83d312, HTTP 200, checked 02:17Z), so the lane meets the artifact the way a stranger would. Attaching the file, or attaching this register, would have told it whose the artifact is in the same breath as asking it to judge blind.

measurement.was_queued_behind: codex/INBOX.md carried task 2026-08-10.a, then .b, and the lane holds exactly one task at a time — scripts/inbox-task.mjs parses a single yaml header. That is a real throughput limit on the pool that is NOT scarce, and RUNBOOK 3 tells laps to file codex_lane candidates with no limit on the number. The document and the mechanism disagree, and this round waited two laps on the difference. Recorded rather than fixed: a queue in the INBOX is a change to the lane, not to this offer, and one lap changes one thing.
measurement.who_must_not_do_it: Whoever wrote the artifact. The rule that makes a stranger reaction worth anything is that the reviewer is not the author, and the Codex lane WROTE assets/free-demo/index.html. So the reviewer must be told nothing about where it came from, and if the lane recognises it the round is void — say so rather than keeping the verdict.

blind_held.so: VALID. The round is kept. Had it read ある or たぶんある the round would have been void and discarded, because the Codex lane wrote assets/free-demo/index.html and an author's opinion cannot answer this rung.
blind_held.what_was_disclosed: the public URL and nothing else — no repository, no authorship, no reason for asking.

rounds.strongest_objection_verbatim: タップして増えるUIは見えたが、購入価値（何を買って何が得られるか）に直接つながる要素が体験内で確認できず、今の状態では有料化判断に必要な納得点が取れなかった。
rounds.strongest_objection_in_english: The tap-to-increment UI was visible, but nothing inside the experience connected to what would actually be bought, so there was no basis on which to judge paying for it.

engagement.depth_verbatim: ページを開いて初期画面を確認し、そこで止めた
engagement.depth: Opened the page, looked at the opening screen, stopped there. Did not play.

rounds.moved_note: Nothing was changed before this round, so there is no prior figure for it to move from. This is the baseline, and the first completed round in this file's history. Rule 4's no-move counter deliberately does not start here: a round that attempted nothing cannot be evidence that a parameter stopped working.

how_much_this_carries.the_default_was_the_answer: The task states the default verdict is 払わない and that only a number overturns it. A reviewer who stopped at the opening screen therefore returned the default, and a returned default is weaker evidence than a refusal after real play. Do NOT let a later lap upgrade this to 'measured: strangers will not pay for it'.
how_much_this_carries.what_it_does_establish: The entrance did not hold one blind reader past the first screen. That is a statement about the opening, which is the part the route depends on most: this artifact is the free door the whole route walks people through.
how_much_this_carries.what_it_does_not_establish: Anything about the paid kit, whose source does not exist anywhere and which nobody has ever opened. The two are routinely named in one breath and the relationship does not exist.
how_much_this_carries.grade: one blind reviewer, self-reported engagement, no instrumentation — the same grade as the lane's other sweeps, and weaker than a behavioural reading would be.

rounds.what_this_does_to_the_elected_route: route_4_the_offer_form_is_the_binding_term names its prerequisite as AN ARTIFACT SOMEONE WHO DID NOT MAKE IT WOULD PAY FOR. Round 1 returns the opposite on the only artifact we own outright. The prerequisite is NOT satisfied and the route is not thereby refuted — one round is not a verdict on the route, and this lap deliberately does not re-elect. Three elections in three days would say the elections are noise.

offers.why_it_is_here_at_all: It is the only thing this account offers that can enter a loop. If the owner's rule is right — and nothing here contradicts it — then this is where demand can actually be built, and the priced product's un-loopability is the reason the two have to be ranked against each other rather than assumed complementary.

void_rounds.why_void: 見覚え: ある. The reviewer recognised the page. state/product-loop.json has said since this rung was declared that a recognised round is VOID and discarded, and the rule is on the ANSWER rather than the cause.
void_rounds.and_this_is_the_hard_part: It is the best round this offer has ever had. All five steps completed, two items exchanged, 25 taps, the per-second rate change observed (0 -> 0.2 -> 0.4), the most-wanted-again moment named (the instant idle income started), the most boring moment named (grinding to 15 by hand), and a specific reason for 払わない: nothing branches and nothing permanent accumulates. Round 1 was criticised for being none of that. Discarding it is what the rule is FOR - a rule that only bites data you did not want is not a rule.
void_rounds.what_must_not_happen: Do not cite any of the content above as a stranger reaction, and do not count it toward rounds or rounds_engaged. It is recorded in this much detail so a later lap can see what was given up, not so the verdict can be smuggled back in.

cause.what: THE TASK TEXT LEAKED. codex/INBOX.md task 2026-08-10.f opened with 前回この依頼を出したとき、返ってきたのは「初期画面を見て止めた」でした - telling the reviewer the page had been reviewed before, while explaining why the instructions were stricter.
cause.so_not_this: The lane is NOT burned. codex exec runs stateless, so recognition could not have come from memory of round 1; it came from the sentence. A blind round on this artifact is still possible, which is the opposite of what the raw 見覚え ある reading suggests.
cause.the_rule_already_existed: measurement.no_longer_queued.how_the_blind_is_kept: the task carries the public URL and nothing else, no repository name, no authorship, no statement of why it is being asked. Prose, unread by any machine. Fourth instance of that shape this session.
cause.the_general_form: The blind was broken by the lap explaining itself. The sentence was added by a lap correctly fixing round 1 weakness, and it reads as helpful context right up until it costs the round.
cause.now_mechanical: scripts/product-loop.mjs blindLeaks() and roundRecognised(); tests/run-tests.mjs asserts the live INBOX text is clean and that a recognised round cannot sit in rounds.

what_this_file_must_not_become: A list of what is already being offered. state/options.json decayed exactly that way on 2026-08-08 — every registry enumerated existing assets, so no amount of turning them could ever conclude 'this portfolio is wrong'. An offer that fails its loop is supposed to be able to leave.
